beats.say: An admin account is the key attackers want most. With a single admin account they can reach the whole network.
Use a normal account for daily work and a separate one for administration. Never read email or browse as admin.
Keep passwords and keys out of code, chats and tickets. They linger there for years. Use a secrets vault instead.

beats.say: Fake support callers often ask you to install a remote-control tool. Then they open the system with your hands.
For admin panels, remote access and cloud consoles, turn on phishing-resistant multi-factor sign-in, such as a physical security key.

scenes.prompt: Find the signs of phishing aimed at admins.

subject.text: Critical: your admin account will be suspended in 2 hours

body.text: Re-register multi-factor sign-in for your tenant.
Then read the confirmation code to the support agent who calls you.

spots.label: Wrong domain
spots.explain: Provider notices come from the provider's own domain. Always open the console from your own bookmark.

spots.label: Suspension threat
spots.explain: A two-hour deadline is there to leave no time to check.

spots.label: Fake sign-in page
spots.explain: This page can relay your password and code in real time. Ordinary codes do not stop that.

spots.label: Reading a code to someone
spots.explain: Real support never asks for your confirmation code. Saying it hands over the account.

question.prompt: Vendor support calls and wants remote access to a server. What do you do?

options.label: I hang up and call the number in the contract
options.feedback: Correct. Verify through a channel you know, then grant access only through the approved tool.

options.label: I install the tool they name and read out the code
options.feedback: That gives the caller full access to the system. Remote-control tools are abused in attacks exactly this way.

options.label: I allow it but watch the screen
options.feedback: Watching is not enough. A backdoor takes seconds to plant.

scenes.explain: An unexpected remote access request is always verified on a known channel and granted only through the approved tool.

body.text: I put the server password in the comments so the next shift can see it.

cards.explain: Many people see tickets and they stay in the archive. Rotate the password and move it to the vault.

body.text: I added the key to the secrets vault and gave you read access.

cards.explain: The key itself is not in the chat, only access in the vault. That is the right way.
The .env file was committed to the repository. Keys stay in history, so deleting the file is not enough. Rotate them now.

body.text: From Monday, admin panel sign-in requires a physical key. Collect yours in person from room 305.

cards.explain: No link, nothing to download or type, the key is handed over in person. This change makes you safer.

body.text: I am off on holiday, here is my admin password, use it if needed.

cards.explain: With a shared admin account no one can tell who did what. The stand-in should get temporary rights on their own account.

scenes.prompt: Match each task to the right account.
scenes.explain: Give each task only the rights it needs. The less an admin account is used, the smaller the target.

nodes.text: It is 02:00. Your phone shows a sign-in approval request for your admin account, and you were asleep.

choices.label: I deny it and alert the security team
choices.feedback: Right. An unexpected prompt means someone knows your password.

choices.label: I approve it so the prompts stop
choices.feedback: The attacker is in the admin panel. This is called a push bombing attack.

nodes.text: Have you used this password anywhere else?
nodes.speaker: Security team
nodes.spoken: Have you used this password <short pause> anywhere else?

choices.label: Yes, on a personal account too. I will change both
choices.feedback: An honest answer. Passwords leaked from other sites are often tried exactly like this.

choices.label: I am embarrassed and say nothing
choices.feedback: The team cannot find the source of the leak. Honesty speeds up the investigation.

nodes.text: The password is changed. What is next?

choices.label: I end active sessions and move the account to a physical key
choices.feedback: Excellent. Ending sessions cuts any open access, and a physical key resists phishing.

choices.label: All good, I get back to work
choices.feedback: Open sessions and tokens may still be alive. Close them too.

points: Admin work on an admin account, daily work on a normal one.
Keep secrets out of code and chats, rotate any leak at once.
Verify unexpected remote access requests on a known channel.
